placements.title: Operational Systems and Their Maintenance
placements.frame: What practices, structures, and rehearsals keep systems recoverable and reliable over time?
placements.why: The document's content is entirely about an operational practice — rollback rehearsals, their cadence, their ownership, and the principle that unrehearsed capabilities are not real. Nothing existing in strata or structure holds this; the content calls for an organizational category for operational systems and their maintenance.

placements.title: From Having a Capability to Having Verified It
placements.frame: Does possession of an operational capability require rehearsal to be real — is the gap between having and having tested constitutive rather than incidental?
placements.why: src-2 mandates monthly rollback rehearsals as a recurring cadence by directive; src-3 crystallizes the rationale into a maxim equating an unrehearsed rollback with a nonexistent one. Together they assert that rehearsal is constitutive of capability, not merely confirmatory — a thematic statement true beyond this document's specific rollback context.

placements.title: From Directive to Operational Fact
placements.frame: How does structured record-keeping convert an authority's spoken directive into settled operational reality?
placements.why: src-4 and src-5 transcribe the directive's cadence and ownership into structured metadata fields, performing the ratification that converts a spoken mandate into an institutional fact. The theme — that records operationalize authority — is true beyond this specific document and will accumulate support as future envelopes document decisions.
